sentences.text: ICAC surveyed 515 NSW adults, mainly in October 1995, to inform its education and corruption prevention work.
sentences.support:
A 
representative sample of 515 NSW adults participated in the telephone survey

sentences.text: The telephone survey examined public sector services and integrity, views of corruption, possible reporting avenues and support for ICAC.
sentences.support:
avenues available to individuals to take action about corruption; and the work of 
the ICAC.

sentences.text: ICAC reported that 58% considered public sector corruption a major problem, compared with 44% in the 1994 survey.
sentences.support:
Fifty-eight per cent of the respondents considered that corruption in the NSW public 
sector is a major problem

sentences.text: ICAC reported that 71% expected people reporting corruption to suffer, while half believed they could do nothing personally about it.
sentences.support:
Fifty per cent of 
respondents agreed that There is nothing I can personally do about corruption in the 
NSW public sector

findings.quote: Public support for the ICAC has remained consistently high.

Members of the public in NSW appear to strongly support both a 
corruption prevention and an education role for the ICAC, in addition to its investigative 
function.

notes: These are respondents' beliefs and ICAC's interpretation of survey responses. No numbered recommendations list.
